issues.description: The problem statement and template expect Course initializer to be called with parameter labels (name:, instructor:, ratings:) and the template declares init(name: String, instructor: String, ratings: [Int]). The solution's Course initializer, however, declares init(instructor: String, name: String, ratings: [Int]) (instructor and name swapped). This mismatch in parameter order/labels is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about the correct initializer signature and how to instantiate Course as shown in the exercise examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Course initializer parameter labels and order consistent across artifacts. Change the solution's initializer to match the problem/template signature: init(name: String, instructor: String, ratings: [Int]) { ... } so students can instantiate Course(name: ..., instructor: ..., ratings: ...) as described in the problem statement.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template show the Course initializer labeled as init(name:instructor:ratings:) (the hint uses Course(name: "My Course", instructor: "My Instructor", ratings: [])), but the solution defines the initializer with the parameter labels reversed: init(instructor:name:ratings:). Although the parameter names themselves are the same, the differing external parameter label order between template/problem and solution creates a mapping mismatch that can confuse students comparing the artifacts and expecting the initializer signature shown in the instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the initializer parameter labels consistent across artifacts. Change the solution initializer to init(name: String, instructor: String, ratings: [Int]) so it matches the problem hint and the template (or, alternatively, update the template/problem hint to use init(instructor:name:ratings:) if that ordering is intentional). Consistent labeling will reduce student confusion when mapping requirements to code.
